questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can injure an infant or small child, even in a minor collision.
Make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt before driving. Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit in the back seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat if there is a front airbag.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but hurts judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but hurts driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also damages your ability to judge speed and distance. Alcohol makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: When you signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from a curb:

options.text: It is only necessary if other cars are nearby.
It is a good habit and the law requires it.
It is only necessary during the move, not before.
It is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Always signal well before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What does alcohol do?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and reduces skills needed for safe driving. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: To avoid tiredness on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Alternate feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take a short break every two hours. If you feel drowsy, pull over to a safe place and take a nap or get a room for the night.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Reduce the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both stronger. Driving after alcohol or drugs is dangerous. Mixing them together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand in traffic lanes or you could be hit. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Keep driving until the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals help other drivers know what you plan to do and prevent accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs only mean a no passing zone.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: When other drivers act angrily, stay away from them. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures that might upset them. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever you can safely do to avoid danger.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot for any vehicles before you move.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: The light is changing from green to red.
The car in front of you is going too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is changing from green to red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the traffic signal is about to turn red. Slow down and prepare to stop. You can only continue if you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely before entering it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a stop sign is ahead and you should prepare to stop completely.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Stop and ask a police officer for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take the next exit.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Never stop, back up, make sudden lane changes, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is coming up.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Fits snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Stops the seat belt warning light from working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get revenge makes the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: They drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than normal traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder whenever you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you and another vehicle arrive at the same time. The other vehicle is to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Slow down and let that vehicle pass through safely before you proceed.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In a crash, stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. Check for injuries and call 911 if anyone is hurt. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 (or over $200 in damage to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be prepared to stop your vehicle to protect the pedestrian from harm.

questions.question: You had a upsetting incident at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Have drinks at a bar before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you feel upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous and puts you and others at risk.
